message.content: FASTCYCLE fixture prompt body (T106, golden-bad, dispatch 2 of 2, class FC-PFX-A -- per-item timestamp placed BEFORE the subset, breaking the shared [core][subset] byte-prefix). No cache read is possible: the provider only serves a cache read when the prefix up to the cache breakpoint is byte-identical to a previously cached prefix (Anthropic prompt caching, R5:20-24); a leading per-item timestamp that differs from dispatch 1's makes that comparison fail at byte 0 of the cached segment. Not a real dispatch.

content.text: T106 fixture (golden-bad): dispatch 2's own first turn -- SAME class as dispatch 1 by classification, but its prompt ordering places the per-item timestamp BEFORE [core][subset], so the byte prefix it actually sends to the provider does NOT match dispatch 1's cached prefix at all. Genuine cache MISS: reads nothing back (cache_read_input_tokens=0, NOT the 1500 the good_order scenario's dispatch 2 reads), pays full price and creates its own fresh cache entry instead (cache_creation_input_tokens=1500).
